what: update_handoff's 120 s status recount went through records(), which reset every record's write watermark to the fresh disk copy, so a later write_record from the phase's load-time rec read its stale values as authored and reverted other writers' description repairs, bands, exclusions and synthesis while returning True.
how: Reproduced in scratch (load -> other writer edits -> update_handoff recount -> stale batch write: description, magnitude and synthesis all reverted, landed True). Root fix in records(): a thread-local _LISTING.only flag makes a read-only listing skip _remember_top_keys; update_handoff sets it around its recount (a flag rather than a parameter because drill stubs records with zero-arg lambdas, e.g. _net_073752d048bc; thread-local so a loader on another thread keeps its watermark). Loaders that write back are unchanged. Side effect: the recount no longer pays the fingerprint pass (N10). Existing watermark, CAS, handoff, phase 1/2/8 drill nets re-run green against the fixed code.

what: write_record's companion clear popped a disk rejection (scale_note_rejected etc.) for every paired entry whenever the stale in-memory entry lacked it, deleting the rejection repass_bands had just preserved.
how: Reproduced. The pop now needs an authored absence: with a watermark it is skipped when the rejection was already absent when the caller loaded the entry; a rejection the caller loaded and then popped still clears on disk; no watermark keeps the old behaviour. The net covers both the preserved and the deliberate-clear case.

what: build() read the corpus and then designations() read it again, overwriting LAST_UNREADABLE, so a record torn in pass 1 and healed by pass 2 let main --write land a short index at rc 0.
how: Reproduced. build() now calls designations(recs) over the list it already holds (an explicit list is never cached), so LAST_UNREADABLE describes the pass the index was built from.
